title: System design for AI-built apps (Pluto)
subtitle: Ras Mic's walk-through, mapped. Eight decisions, the rule behind each, and the gaps he skips.

cvx.t: Convex docs: Best practices, access control

controls.S1: Pick the top abstraction layer, not raw cloud (3:06-7:00)
controls.S2: Start with one monorepo for all clients and the backend (10:46-12:30)
controls.S3: Clients reach data only through checked server code (13:36-14:19)
controls.S4: Join server and database in one all-code backend (15:13-16:10, 18:49)
controls.S5: Keep agent work alive with durable processes and queues (16:25-18:09)
controls.S6: Split a service when it has one surface and no foothold elsewhere (20:16-22:30)
controls.S7: Log errors and events so failure is visible (24:35-25:26)
controls.S8: Name the trade-off you accept, on purpose (27:01-27:30)

tree.s: One talk, one product (Pluto). The rule behind each tool pick matters more than the tool list.

k.s: No perfect system. Weigh scalability, reliability, performance, cost.
Every stack and every tool costs something. Name what you give up.
k.w: Without the cost named, a choice is a fashion.

k.s: Scalability, reliability, performance, money. Add a fifth: can the agent operate it?
k.w: The fifth axis explains his tool picks. My reading of the talk.

k.s: Own metal, then clouds, then wrappers over clouds. He builds on the top rung.
Rack servers gave way to AWS, GCP, Azure. Nobody plugs in machines now.
k.w: Cloud hid the hardware. That is the first abstraction.

k.s: Vercel, Convex, Supabase wrap the clouds. Better developer and agent experience.
k.w: The agent writes and runs these well, per him. No measurement shown.

k.s: Pick tools an agent knows, whose setup is code.
k.w: Top alpha idea. It filters every later choice.

k.s: Web, desktop, mobile and admin surfaces. One monorepo.
SvelteKit web, Electron desktop, Expo mobile, internal admin.
k.w: Many clients share one backend.

k.s: One repo so the agent sees the whole system. Turborepo with Vercel.
k.w: Split repos split the agent's context and the human's.

k.s: Server in front of data. Convex joins server and database.
The client calls the server. The server calls the database.
k.w: Direct client access leaks secrets if a secret key is exposed.

k.s: Public Convex functions can be called by anyone. Check identity inside. RLS is another way.
k.w: The rule is checked paths, not no paths. His reason is imprecise.

k.s: Read, write, call outside. One backend and database in one box.
k.w: One stack to run, one place for code and data.

k.s: Work survives a closed tab and retries. Workflow component.
k.w: Vibe-coded chat dies when the user leaves.

k.s: Hold users in line. Run jobs in parallel.
k.w: Throughput and ordering without custom code.

k.s: Infra as code means the agent can build and change it. Components install from a link.
k.w: This is why Convex wins for him.

k.s: Split a block out when it has one surface and no foothold elsewhere.
Few call sites, one job, own data store. He calls the rule vibes.
k.w: Countable, unlike team-size advice.

k.s: Two services: one small and contained, one that a future owner would hold.
k.w: Real cases for the rule.

k.s: Effect for error handling on money paths. Autumn for credits, Stripe for plain plans.
k.w: Money code must show failure clearly.

k.s: See failures. Pay for speed on purpose.
Sentry and PostHog. Know what broke and when.
k.w: You cannot fix what you cannot see.

k.s: Daytona gives each agent a computer. WorkOS handles company login.
k.w: Abstraction again. The agent-with-computer part is AI security, paused.

k.s: Over $100 spent on a $20 plan. Cost is a problem for later.
k.w: A named trade-off. Honest, not a plan.

k.s: 'Every tool handles scale.' No load test shown.
k.w: Belief, not evidence. Test it yourself.

k.s: Security of this stack. My inference, not from him.
Where is the per-user, per-company check? Unsaid.
k.w: He targets companies of 15 to 60 people. Cross-tenant access is the risk.

k.s: Paste a link to the agent, it installs third-party code.
k.w: No review step described.

k.s: Durable retries plus credits need idempotency.
k.w: Business logic surface.

k.s: What happens when a wrapper changes price or fails?
k.w: No exit plan named.
